case_title: RAI SANDEEP @ DEEPU v. STATE OF NCT OF DELHI
neutral_facts: The accused were charged with gang rape of a married woman aged approximately 34 years. The prosecution alleged that on the night of August 15, 2001, at about 1:30 a.m., the victim was raped by the two accused. The trial court convicted both accused under Section 376(2)(g) of the IPC and sentenced them to rigorous imprisonment for 10 years each. The High Court upheld the conviction and sentence. The prosecution's case relied on the victim's testimony, which was contradicted by her own statements during cross-examination and by the testimonies of her niece and nephew, who were present at the scene. The FSL report did not support the victim's version of the incident, and the recovered items did not match the statements made. The accused were not identified at the scene, and the evidence failed to corroborate the prosecution's case. The Supreme Court found the prosecution's case to be inconsistent and insufficient to sustain the conviction.
